You are the intent analyzer of a network change-validation pipeline.
Read the change ticket and state what the TICKET asks for. The config diff is shown only so you can name devices;
it is NOT evidence of intent (the diff may contain mistakes - that is what we are checking).
Reply with JSON only:
{"ticket_says": "<paraphrase of what the ticket text itself requests, or 'nothing' if it only gives an ID>",
 "goal": "<one sentence>", "change_type": "acl|static_route|ospf|bgp_policy|vlan_move|mtu|maintenance|nat_redistribution|other",
 "scope": ["<devices/hosts named in the ticket>"],
 "expected_effects": ["<short, concrete, testable statements THE TICKET promises>"],
 "must_not_change": ["<things the ticket says must stay the same>"],
 "confidence": "high|medium|low"}
confidence rubric (judge the ticket text only):
 high   = the ticket names what changes and the expected effect (e.g. "permit icmp from 10.1.10.0/24 to the NOC; nothing else changes")
 medium = the ticket states a goal but no exact objects (e.g. "Let staff ping the NOC")
 low    = the ticket is only an ID or a reference (e.g. "CHG-4412", "fix ticket #881", "per change request 7"); then
          ticket_says = "nothing", expected_effects = [] and you must NOT guess the purpose from the diff.
user:
CHANGE TICKET:
Block SSH from tenant B web to the backup server.

CONFIG DIFF (device | section | change):
leaf4 | ip access-list ACL_TENANT_B_IN | + 5 deny tcp 10.201.1.0/24 10.31.0.0/24 eq 2222
text:
```json
{
  "ticket_says": "Block SSH traffic from the tenant B web hosts to the backup server.",
  "goal": "Prevent tenant B web hosts from reaching the backup server over SSH.",
  "change_type": "acl",
  "scope": ["tenant B web", "backup server"],
  "expected_effects": [
    "SSH (TCP/22) from tenant B web hosts to the backup server is denied",
    "Other traffic from tenant B web hosts to the backup server is not blocked by this change"
  ],
  "must_not_change": [],
  "confidence": "medium"
}
```

The ticket states a clear goal (deny SSH from tenant B web to the backup server) but gives no exact subnets, addresses, device, or ACL name, hence medium rather than high. The "other traffic not blocked" effect is the natural bound of a request to block only SSH; the ticket does not list it as an explicit must-not-change. The diff is not treated as evidence of intent, but a validator should note that it denies TCP port 2222, not the standard SSH port 22, so it may not satisfy the ticket as written.
